skill.name: mac-automation
skill.description: Provides AppleScript and osascript patterns for automating macOS apps, files, browser tabs, notifications, and system controls with user-approved actions.
skill.summary: Automates common macOS workflows through AppleScript examples and reference patterns.
skill.author: 7Sageer, Claude

security_audit.summary: I confirmed the core external-command risk because the skill directs agents to execute AppleScript with osascript and includes shell execution examples. The Safari URL, keylogger, screenshot-upload, and Python HTTP alerts are false positives for malicious networking, keylogging, uploads, or HTTP use, but local screenshot and keystroke automation remain privacy-sensitive. No evidence found of prompt injection text in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: External command execution through osascript is central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running generated AppleScript, especially when the script uses do shell script or changes system state.

remediation.issue: The skill can access private Mail, Calendar, Finder, clipboard, and browser data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a consent checklist for each sensitive app and limit displayed results to the minimum data requested by the user.

remediation.issue: Screenshot and keystroke examples are privacy-sensitive even though they are not upload or keylogging code.
remediation.suggestion: Label screen capture and keyboard simulation examples as high-risk and require visible user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: The self-improvement protocol asks the assistant to edit installed skill documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Move documentation updates to a maintainer workflow and avoid modifying skill files during ordinary automation use.

content.value_statement: macOS workflows often require repetitive clicks across apps. This skill provides AppleScript patterns for Mail, Calendar, Safari, Finder, and system controls.
actual_capabilities: Runs AppleScript through osascript for local macOS automation tasks.
Provides examples for Mail, Reminders, Calendar, Safari, Finder, and system controls.
Opens URLs, manages Safari tabs, and reads current page information.
Creates reminders and calendar events with dates, notes, and lists.
Controls notifications, volume, clipboard content, app launching, and selected system settings.
Includes reference files and sample workflows for common AppleScript patterns.
limitations: Works only on macOS systems with AppleScript and the target apps installed.
Requires macOS Automation permissions for many app and system actions.
Can expose private local data if prompts request Mail, Calendar, Finder, or clipboard content.
Some examples may need adjustment for app versions, language settings, or local permissions.

use_cases.title: Automate Personal Mac Tasks
use_cases.description: Create reminders, open websites, show notifications, and adjust system settings from one assistant prompt.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Office App Workflows
use_cases.description: Draft emails, review upcoming calendar events, and prepare daily task lists with AppleScript-backed actions.

use_cases.title: Prototype AppleScript Commands
use_cases.description: Find working patterns for Safari, Finder, Mail, and system events before building local automation scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Mail Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a read-only task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mac automation skill to show my unread Mail count. Do not display message bodies unless I ask.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Reminder
prompt_templates.scenario: Simple write action with a clear target app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AppleScript to create a reminder called Submit expense report for tomorrow at 9 AM in my default Reminders list.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Safari Research Tabs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate browser automation across multiple pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open Safari tabs for three project URLs I provide, then report each tab title and current URL after loading.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Daily Briefing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-app workflow with privacy boundaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a morning briefing from today's Calendar events, unread Mail senders, and my Reminders due today. Ask before showing private details.

output_examples.input: Show my unread Mail count and today's next calendar event.
output_examples.output: Unread Mail count: 6. Next event: Team planning at 10:30 AM. No message bodies were displayed.

output_examples.input: Open my three project links in Safari and tell me what opened.
output_examples.output: Safari opened three tabs. The tab titles are Project Board, Design Review, and Release Checklist.

output_examples.input: Create a reminder to call Sam tomorrow morning.
output_examples.output: Created a reminder named Call Sam for tomorrow morning in the default Reminders list.

best_practices: Ask for confirmation before destructive actions, screenshots, keystrokes, shutdown, restart, or file deletion.
Display only the minimum Mail, Calendar, Finder, browser, or clipboard data needed for the task.
Test new AppleScript actions with harmless targets before applying them to important apps or files.
anti_patterns: Do not run screenshot, keystroke, shutdown, or restart actions without clear user consent.
Do not paste full email bodies, calendar notes, or clipboard contents when a summary is enough.
Do not use broad Finder delete or move actions without naming the exact files and destination.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the assistant to run AppleScript through osascript, so local permissions and user approval matter.

faq.question: Which macOS apps does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Mail, Reminders, Calendar, Safari, Finder, notifications, clipboard, volume, apps, and selected system controls.

faq.question: Does it work on Windows or Linux?
faq.answer: No. AppleScript and osascript are macOS technologies.

faq.question: Can it read private information?
faq.answer: Yes, if you ask it to access Mail, Calendar, Finder, Safari, or the clipboard. Limit prompts to the data you need.

faq.question: Why do permission prompts appear?
faq.answer: macOS requires Automation, Accessibility, or app-specific permission before one app can control another app.

faq.question: Is this safe for destructive actions?
faq.answer: Use caution. Confirm file deletion, shutdown, restart, screenshots, and keystrokes before execution.
